summary: clone-free count-based outlier filter + branchless validation BCE; +6% bit-for-bit output
comment: 4-way bundle, +6% median (pairs 1.0611/1.0595), BIT-FOR-BIT output (0/50 raw+4dp; benchmark.py authoritative = 0/50 params + 0/50 LogLoss, mean 0.313500 d=0; frozen compute_parameters re-verified 0/50 vs committed cp record). (1) COUNT-BASED outlier filter (training.rs compute_outlier_removed_pairs): old code items.clone()'d ALL items to extract cnt==1 init candidates + stored Vec<FSRSItem> per (rating,delta_t) bucket + extend_from_slice'd a filtered_items init set that EVERY caller discards. The threshold logic only reads bucket SIZES, so rewrote to take impl Iterator<Item=&FSRSItem> and tally COUNTS (HashMap<u32,HashMap<u32,usize>>) -> ZERO init clone, no item storage. Updated filter_outlier (pub; kept sig, returns empty init), prepare_training_data (inline, no clone), prepare_training_data_carded (no clone), preserving each fn's distinct no-outlier trainset behaviour. STRUCTURAL bit-for-bit (removed_pairs byte-identical). Subsumes the earlier clone-trim+filtered-skip probes. ~+3-3.5% alone. (2) Branchless validation BCE (Andrew's -ln(1-|label-r|)): batch_loss_simd loss -> ONE vectorized ln8::<false> vs r.to_array()+8 scalar f64 lns; PRECISION but 0/50 (robust best-epoch argmin, error<<epoch gaps). ~+2.4%. Andrew chose 'push for margin' over the borderline 3-way +5.0%; count-based pushed it to confident +6%. cplx 7296->7299 (thr 1.001). champion .pyd /tmp/bench_iter2v2.pyd=/tmp/bench_champ.pyd 3d1147ed.
